$comment: Hard npm-tarball budgets against the measured pre-8.0.0 baseline. Packed and unpacked ceilings are set from current measurements with 5% headroom, then ratchet downward when real reductions land; an unmet fixed reduction target would leave the gate permanently red. Ratcheted forward once already: a broad accessibility/correctness remediation sweep across roughly five dozen components (the same sweep that required re-budgeting the packed-consumer core bundle check) grew the measured package to 6,630,349 packed / 28,329,498 unpacked bytes and 3,115 files, past the prior ceilings. The file ceiling is the prior 2,500-artifact limit plus two emitted files for each of 284 stable lr-* alias entries (283 -> 284: one new component) and 72 files of entrypoint headroom (34 -> 72: the remainder of the measured growth, not attributable to the alias count alone); explicit source/map rejection remains independent. Ratcheted forward a second time: web-types.json now carries the js/properties, js/events and slots projections it previously omitted entirely (0 of 284 tags had any of the three), which is the metadata JetBrains completion reads for the `.prop=`/`@event=` binding style these Lit components are actually used with. That projection is ~1.78 MiB unpacked (~205 KiB gzip) of genuinely new information, not bloat, so the unpacked ceiling is re-set from the new measurement with the same 5% headroom. The packed ceiling is deliberately NOT raised -- packed still fits under it, and loosening a gate that is not red discards real signal. The alias count moves 284 -> 285 for lr-funnel. Packed ceiling ratcheted at the 12.0.0 release: the version stamp and CHANGELOG additions put the tarball 660 bytes over the previous 6,961,867 ceiling (6,962,527 measured). That ceiling was deliberately left alone when the unpacked one moved earlier in this release, because packed still fit at the time -- it no longer does, and this is the same measure-then-add-5%-headroom rule, not a relaxation: the new ceiling stays well under the 7,829,794 baseline validatePackageBudgets asserts against. Version-bump growth tripping these budgets on the release commit itself is a known step, documented in the release runbook.
